title: NEHA AGGARWAL versus STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
THE HON'BLE CHIEF JUSTICE MR. MANOJ KUMAR GUPTA
AND
THE HON'BLE JUSTICE MR. SUBHASH UPADHYAY
Writ Petition (S/B) No.640 of 2026
30th September, 2026
Neha Aggarwal -----Petitioner
Versus
State of Uttarakhand and Others ----Respondents
-----------------------------------------------------------------
Presence:-
Mr. M.C. Pant, learned counsel for the petitioner.
Mr. Sachin Mohan Singh Mehta, learned Standing Counsel for the
State of Uttarakhand.
-----------------------------------------------------------------
JUDGMENT : (per Mr. Manoj Kumar Gupta C. J.)
1. Heard learned counsel for the parties.
2. The present writ petition has been filed assailing
the transfer order dated 24.09.2026 and the
consequential relieving order dated 25.09.2026 issued by
the respondent authorities whereby the petitioner, who is
presently serving as Assistant Professor in the Department
of Physiology, Veer Chandra Singh Garhwali (VCSG)
Government Institute of Medical Sciences & Research,
Srinagar Garhwal has been transferred to Government
Medical College Rudrapur.
3. The main ground on which the transfer order
has been challenged is that the petitioner was appointed
and posted at the present place of posting on 07.01.2026
1

and within a short time of eight months she has been
transferred. It is contended that the same is contrary to
the provisions of the Transfer Act, 2017.
4. Learned State Counsel has placed on record the
instructions received from the Directorate of Medical
Education, Uttarakhand. Paragraph nos. 3, 4 and 5 of the
instructions, which are relevant, are as follows:
"3. That in the present writ petition, the petitioner has
self-contradictorily challenged the transfer order No.
1340/XXVIII (5)/2026 (E-31073) dated 24.09.2026
passed by the office of Medical Health & Medical
Education Department, Govt. of Uttarakhand, specifically
mentioning that the mentioned order was received by
her on WhatsApp which she does not consider as 'clear
formal intimation' and that the transfer was directed to
be implemented immediately. It is submitted that the
transfer of the faculties/ staff is a policy matter of Govt.
of Uttarakhand, which is time-to-time implemented
considering the priority of patient welfare and the
academic functioning. Moreover, the petitioner was not
alone to be transfered instead many other faculties were
also transferred to meet NMC requirements for starting
Rudrapur Medical College.
4. That through the present writ petition, the petitioner
has tried to present herself as the victim of
circumstances owing to the transfer order alleging it as
'arbitrary' and 'liable to be quashed' for which she has
presented various reasons including her husband's
posting, her health etc.
5. That the respondent has complied the order which
was to be implemented immediately. Consequently, the
petitioner was relieved on 25.09.2026 complying the
transfer order No. 1340/XXVIII (5)/2026 (E-31073)
dated 24.09.2026."
5. As the petitioner has been transferred to meet
the NMC requirements and to fill up the vacant post of
Assistant Professor in Rudrapur Medical College in the
2

Department of Physiology, therefore, we are not inclined
to interfere with the transfer order.
6. The petitioner holds a transferrable post and
transfer having been made in public interest, there is no
occasion for this Court to interfere with the transfer order.
7. The writ petition lacks merit and the same is,
accordingly, dismissed.
8. At this stage, learned counsel for the petitioner
submits that husband of the petitioner is posted as
Medical Officer, Rudraprayag and it is urged that her
husband be also transferred to Rudrapur.
9. In respect of the said submission, we leave it
open to the petitioner's husband to make representation
before the authorities for his transfer to Rudrapur and, in
the event any such representation is made, the same shall
be considered by the competent authority within two
weeks.
 (MANOJ KUMAR GUPTA, C. J.)
